examples.solution_text:
$\begin{align*}h&=\frac{b-a}{n}\\&=\frac{2-0}{4}\\&=0.5\end{align*}$
The left endpoints are $0,\ 0.5,\ 1,\ 1.5$.
$\begin{align*}A&\approx0.5\left[f(0)+f(0.5)+f(1)+f(1.5)\right]\\&=0.5(3+3.25+4+5.25)\\&=7.75\text{ square units}\end{align*}$
The function is increasing, so each left-endpoint rectangle lies below the curve. This is an underestimate.

$\begin{align*}h&=\frac{2-0}{4}\\&=0.5\end{align*}$
The right endpoints are $0.5,\ 1,\ 1.5,\ 2$.
$\begin{align*}A&\approx0.5\left[f(0.5)+f(1)+f(1.5)+f(2)\right]\\&=0.5(3.25+4+5.25+7)\\&=9.75\text{ square units}\end{align*}$
The function is increasing, so each right-endpoint rectangle covers the region beneath the curve on its strip. This is an overestimate.

$\begin{align*}h&=\frac{2-0}{4}\\&=0.5\end{align*}$
The first midpoint is $0+\frac{0.5}{2}=0.25$. Adding $0.5$ each time gives $0.25,\ 0.75,\ 1.25,\ 1.75$.
$\begin{align*}A&\approx0.5\left[f(0.25)+f(0.75)+f(1.25)+f(1.75)\right]\\&=0.5(3.0625+3.5625+4.5625+6.0625)\\&=8.625\text{ square units}\end{align*}$

$\begin{align*}h&=\frac{3-0}{3}\\&=1\text{ s}\end{align*}$
The left endpoints are $t=0,\ 1,\ 2$. Since velocity is positive, the area under the velocity-time graph gives the distance travelled.
$\begin{align*}d&\approx h\left[v(0)+v(1)+v(2)\right]\\&=1(10+11+14)\\&=35\text{ m}\end{align*}$

examples.derivation: Width (2−0)/4=0.5. Left-endpoint heights are 3, 3.25, 4 and 5.25; their sum is 15.5. Estimated area is 0.5×15.5=7.75 square units. The function increases on the interval, so this underestimates the area. Each drawn rectangle has the correct left-endpoint height.

Width is 0.5. Right-endpoint heights are 3.25, 4, 5.25 and 7; their sum is 19.5. Estimated area is 0.5×19.5=9.75 square units. The increasing function makes this an overestimate. Each drawn rectangle has the correct right-endpoint height.

Width is 0.5 and midpoints are 0.25, 0.75, 1.25 and 1.75. Their heights are 3.0625, 3.5625, 4.5625 and 6.0625, summing to 17.25. Estimated area is 0.5×17.25=8.625 square units. Rectangle heights and marked points agree with the curve.

Width (3−0)/3=1 second. Left-endpoint velocities at t=0, 1 and 2 are 10, 11 and 14 metres per second. Estimated distance is 1×(10+11+14)=35 metres. Velocity stays positive, so accumulated displacement equals distance. The three rectangles match these velocities.
